questions.prompt: Writing KCL for the CS stage's high-frequency model, how many node equations are needed, and what order is the denominator?
options: Two (gate and drain), giving a second-order denominator
Three, one per capacitor, giving third order
None; the gain is \(-g_mR_o\) at all frequencies
questions.explanation: The gate and drain are the two unknown nodes (reader Eqs. 14.11 and 14.12). Three capacitors in a loop store only two independent states.

questions.prompt: The CS stage has \(g_m = 2\ \mathrm{mS}\) and \(C_{gd} = 5\ \mathrm{fF}\). Where is its transfer-function zero, in GHz?
questions.explanation: The numerator is \(g_m - sC_{gd}\), so \(\omega_z = g_m/C_{gd}\) and \(f_z = 63.7\ \mathrm{GHz}\) (reader Eq. 14.16). It is in the right half plane.

questions.prompt: Why is the CS stage's zero in the right half plane?
options: At \(\omega_z\) the current fed forward through \(C_{gd}\) equals \(g_mv_{gs}\) and cancels it with the opposite sign
It is not; the zero is at \(-g_m/C_{gd}\)
questions.explanation: The feed-forward path is non-inverting while the transistor path inverts; when they balance, the output current is zero at a positive real \(s\).

questions.prompt: For the same stage, find the exact \(-3\ \mathrm{dB}\) frequency in MHz.
questions.explanation: With poles far apart, \(f_{-3dB} \approx 1/(2\pi b_1) = 69.2\ \mathrm{MHz}\). The exact value from \(|H(j\omega)|\) is a little higher, 72.8 MHz, because the second pole is not infinitely far away.
questions.figure_alt: Bode magnitude of the CS stage: flat at about 26 dB, a dominant pole near 70 MHz, and a second pole above 1 GHz.

questions.prompt: When is \(\omega_{p1} \approx 1/b_1\) a good estimate of the dominant pole?
options: When the two poles are widely separated, so \(b_1 \approx 1/\omega_{p1}\)
questions.explanation: \(b_1 = 1/\omega_{p1} + 1/\omega_{p2}\); if \(\omega_{p2} \gg \omega_{p1}\) the second term is negligible.

options: The input pole moves to infinity, leaving one pole at \(1/[R_o(C_L + C_{gd})]\)
questions.explanation: With an ideal source the gate is pinned, so \(C_{gs}\) is irrelevant and \(C_{gd}\) just loads the drain.

questions.prompt: Solve \(1 + b_1s + b_2s^2 = 0\) exactly for the same stage. Find the lower pole magnitude as a frequency in MHz.
questions.explanation: \(\omega = [b_1 - \sqrt{b_1^2 - 4b_2}]/(2b_2) = 4.58\times10^8\ \mathrm{rad/s}\), i.e. 73.0 MHz, close to the 69.2 MHz dominant-pole estimate.

questions.explanation: \(1/(2\pi\cdot10\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\cdot10\ \mathrm{pF}) = 1.59\ \mathrm{MHz}\); a large load swamps every other term in \(b_1\).
